objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
1.	Apply combinatorial methods to solve counting problems.
2.	Understand and use the axioms and properties of probability.
3.	Analyze conditional probability and independence.
4.	Model random phenomena using discrete and continuous random variables.
5.	Compute expectations, variances, and higher moments.
6.	Apply common probability distributions to practical problems.
7.	Understand the law of large numbers and central limit theorem.
8.	Gain a basic understanding of Markov chains and stochastic processes.
content: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of probability theory with applications to real-world problems. Topics include combinatorial analysis, axioms of probability, conditional probability, random variables, expectation, common probability distributions, limit theorems, and an introduction to stochastic processes. The course emphasizes problem-solving and critical thinking.
books:
1.	A First Course in Probability (10 版)
Sheldon Ross (華泰書局)
2.	Introduction to Probability, Statistics, and Random Processes by Hossein Pishro-Nik.
